THR.Settings.ModuleEnabled.Name: Enable Tricky Homebrew Rules
THR.Settings.ModuleEnabled.Hint: Master switch for this world. When off, every rule below is inactive regardless of its own setting.
THR.Rules.CriticalDice.Enabled.Name: Critical Dice: Maximize Best Dice
THR.Rules.CriticalDice.Enabled.Hint: On a critical hit, the dice with the most to gain are replaced with their maximum. Selection is by potential gain, not by lowest roll - a 5 on a d12 beats a 1 on a d4. Normal critical dice doubling is unchanged; this applies on top of it.
THR.Rules.CriticalDice.Count.Name: Critical Dice: Dice Maximized
THR.Rules.CriticalDice.Count.Hint: How many dice are maximized on each critical hit. This is the total across the whole crit, not per damage part - a Rogue's weapon dice and Sneak Attack dice compete for the same slots. Default 2.
THR.Rules.CriticalDice.ApplyToNPCs.Name: Critical Dice: Apply to NPCs
THR.Rules.CriticalDice.ApplyToNPCs.Hint: When on (default), every critical hit is upgraded, including monsters'. When off, only player-owned characters benefit.
THR.Rules.MaxHealing.Enabled.Name: Max Healing: Add a Maximize Button
THR.Rules.MaxHealing.Enabled.Hint: Adds a Maximize button to the healing roll dialog, which takes the maximum value instead of rolling. For potions drunk as an action, or any healing while Beacon of Hope is up. Only appears when everything being rolled is healing, so it can never quietly maximize damage as well.
THR.Rules.RollToBonus.Enabled.Name: Roll to Bonus: Apply Rolled Values
THR.Rules.RollToBonus.Enabled.Hint: Adds an Apply as bonus button to chat cards with a roll, turning the rolled number into a temporary bonus to AC, saves, attacks and more. For Swords Bard flourishes, Combat Inspiration, and any homebrew of the shape roll a die and add it to something for a while.
THR.Rules.RollToBonus.NoCombat: No combat is running, so turn-based durations have nothing to count from. The bonus will stay until you remove it by hand.
THR.Rules.RollToBonus.NoRecipient: No one to apply the bonus to. Select or target a token first.
THR.Rules.RollToBonus.NotOwner: You do not have permission to add effects to {name}. Ask the GM to apply it.
THR.Rules.RollToBonus.BadValue: That is not a usable bonus value.
THR.Rules.RollToBonus.Failed: Could not apply the bonus. Check the console (F12).
THR.Rules.SourceNamedEffects.Enabled.Nam: Effect Names: Use the Source Item Name
THR.Rules.SourceNamedEffects.Enabled.Hin: Names applied effects after the item that produced them, so casting Shield gives an effect called Shield rather than Imperceptible Barrier. Also covers passive effects on your characters own items, so a paladin reads Aura of Protection rather than Protected. Conditions, concentration and enchantments keep their own names. Use the button below to convert effects already in your world.
THR.Rules.SourceNamedEffects.Sweep.Name: Rename Existing Effects
THR.Rules.SourceNamedEffects.Sweep.Label: Rename Existing Effects
THR.Rules.SourceNamedEffects.Sweep.Hint: Rename effects already sitting on actors so they match the new naming, instead of leaving your world half converted.
THR.Rules.SourceNamedEffects.Sweep.Confi: Rename every effect in this world to match the item it came from? This edits your actors and their items, including unlinked tokens on every scene, and cannot be undone automatically. Conditions, concentration and enchantments are left alone, and world and compendium items are never touched.
THR.Rules.SourceNamedEffects.Sweep.Done: Renamed {count} effect(s) to match their source item.
THR.Rules.SourceNamedEffects.Sweep.GMOnl: Only the GM can rename existing effects.
THR.Rules.ExpireEffects.Enabled.Name: Expire Effects: Remove Them When Time Runs Out
THR.Rules.ExpireEffects.Enabled.Hint: Nothing in Foundry or dnd5e removes an effect once its duration ends, so bonuses linger forever. This removes them when their time is up. When a concentration spell runs out, the caster stops concentrating and dnd5e removes the effect from every target.
THR.Rules.ExpireEffects.Mode.Name: Expire Effects: What To Do
THR.Rules.ExpireEffects.Mode.Hint: Whether an expired effect is deleted outright or just switched off. Disabling leaves it on the sheet so you can see what happened. Concentration is always deleted regardless, because dnd5e counts a disabled concentration marker as still concentrating, so switching one off would leave the caster silently locked into a spell that has ended.
THR.Rules.ExpireEffects.Mode.Disable: Disable it, but leave it there
THR.Rules.RollToBonus.Scope.Name: Roll to Bonus: Where The Button Appears
THR.Rules.RollToBonus.Scope.Hint: Which chat cards get an Apply as bonus button. Attack rolls never do, since a to-hit number is not a bonus anyone hands out. Bare skill checks and saving throws never do either, because they come from no item.
THR.Rules.RollToBonus.NoRoller: Could not work out who made this roll. Pick Targeted or Selected tokens instead.
THR.Rules.Auras.Enabled.Name: Auras: Apply Effects To Tokens In Range
THR.Rules.Auras.Enabled.Hint: Lets an effect radiate to other tokens within a radius, following them as they move. Configure an aura from the Aura button on any effect. Where two tokens radiate the same aura, only the strongest applies.
THR.Rules.Auras.Config.Title: Aura: {name}
THR.Rules.Auras.Config.RadiusHint: In grid units. A formula works too, so a scaling aura can use something like @abilities.cha.mod * 5.
THR.Rules.Auras.Config.StacksHint: Off by default, matching 5e: two paladins radiating the same aura grant one bonus, the stronger of the two. Turn on for homebrew meant to add up.
THR.Rules.Auras.Config.RememberHint: Adds it to this world's table of known auras. The same settings are then applied automatically whenever an effect with this name turns up again, so a spell aura comes back on every cast, and Set Up Known Auras offers it on any other character with the same feature. Useful for homebrew, which the built-in table cannot know about.
THR.Rules.Auras.Config.Remembered: {name} added to this world's known auras.
THR.Rules.Auras.Config.StrengthHint: Only used to decide which of two same-named auras wins. Left blank, the aura is measured by its own change values, which is usually what you want.
THR.Rules.Auras.Config.Failed: Could not save the aura configuration. Check the console (F12).
THR.Rules.Auras.Setup.Name: Set Up Known Auras
THR.Rules.Auras.Setup.Label: Set Up Known Auras
THR.Rules.Auras.Setup.Hint: Radii are the values at the level the feature is gained. Paladin auras widen to 30 feet at 18th level, so raise those here if they apply. Anything already configured is listed but left unticked.
THR.Rules.Auras.Setup.Intro: These items are recognised as auras. Correct anything that looks wrong, untick anything you do not want, then apply.
THR.Rules.Auras.Setup.NoneFound: No recognised auras found. Homebrew auras still need setting up from the Aura button on their effect.
THR.SelfCheck.Missing: Tricky Homebrew Rules: this version of Foundry or dnd5e has moved something these rules rely on. Affected: {rules}. See the console for detail.
THR.Rules.Auras.HUD.RightClick: Right click to choose individual auras.
THR.Rules.Auras.Config.ShowRadius: Draw its range on the token
THR.Rules.Auras.Config.Transient: This effect was applied by a spell or ability, so it is thrown away and rebuilt from scratch the next time. Settings saved here go with it. Remember this aura is ticked below so they come back on the next cast.
THR.Rules.Auras.Config.Seeded: Filled in from the module's table of known auras. Check the radius before saving, since some auras widen at higher levels.
Effects Panel: Show Effects Beside The Sidebar
Shows what is running on the selected token as icons at the top right. Hover one for the detail, and use the cross to remove it. This is your own setting rather than the table’s.
THR.Rules.EffectsPanel.Settings.Show.Hin: By default only things happening to the creature: spell effects, conditions, concentration and auras reaching it. Permanent kit like Jack of All Trades or a fighting style is left off.
THR.Rules.EffectsPanel.Settings.Show.Tem: Only what is currently happening to it
THR.Rules.EffectsPanel.HintRemove: Click the cross to remove it.
THR.Rules.EffectsPanel.HintDisable: Granted by an item. The cross switches it off.
THR.Rules.EffectsPanel.RemoveFailed: That effect could not be removed.
THR.Rules.EffectsPanel.FromAura: Radiating from {name}. Turn the aura off at its source to remove this.
THR.Rules.SelfEffects.Settings.Enabled.N: Self Effects: Apply Self-Targeted Spells Automatically
THR.Rules.SelfEffects.Settings.Enabled.H: A spell like Shield or Blur has nobody else its effect could go on, so the Apply Effect button asks a question with one answer. Shield in particular is cast in the middle of someone else's attack. Anything that reaches another creature keeps its button: a spell with a range in feet like Bless, an area like Burning Hands, and a feature that rolls against a target like Stunning Strike, whose range reads Self only because the feature has none of its own.
THR.Rules.SelfEffects.Settings.Scope.Hin: Emanations are centred on the caster but reach other creatures. The Auras rule spreads those from the caster's own copy, so including them is usually what you want.
THR.Rules.SelfEffects.Settings.Scope.Cas: Only spells that affect nobody else (Shield, Blur)
THR.Rules.SelfEffects.Settings.Scope.Ema: Also emanations centred on the caster (Aura of Life)
THR.Rules.Auras.Config.CopyRedirect: That is a copy this aura applied, not the aura itself. Opening the original instead, so the settings stick.
THR.Rules.Auras.Config.CopyOrphan: That is a copy of an aura whose original no longer exists. It will be cleared up on the next pass.
THR.Rules.Auras.Config.StyleGroupLight: Foundry light effect (uses the token's light)
THR.Rules.Auras.Config.ColorationHint: Foundry's coloration technique, used only by the light effects. Ignored by the drawn rings.
THR.Rules.Auras.Config.StyleHint: Drawn rings are painted by this module and cost nothing. Light effects use Foundry's own shaders and look far better, but a token has only one light: the widest aura gets it, the token's own light is given back when no aura needs it, and they emit no illumination and reveal nothing.
THR.Rules.Auras.Config.ColourHint: The colour of the range ring drawn on the token. Automatic uses yellow for auras that reach allies and red for ones that reach enemies. Pick a colour to tell overlapping auras apart.
